name: DBpedia SPARQL Endpoint
summary: Public SPARQL endpoint over DBpedia, the knowledge graph extracted from Wikipedia infoboxes and categories, free and keyless.
description: DBpedia turns structured parts of Wikipedia into linked data: entities with labels, abstracts, types, infobox properties and links to other datasets. The endpoint at dbpedia.org/sparql answers SPARQL SELECT, ASK and CONSTRUCT queries over HTTP GET or POST, and every resource also has a JSON, RDF or HTML description under dbpedia.org/data.

rate_limit.summary: Not documented; a result cap of 10000 rows per query is sent in the X-SPARQL-MaxRows header.

endpoints.summary: Run a SPARQL query; choose the result format with the format parameter
Same with a form-encoded body, for long queries
All triples about one resource as JSON (also .rdf, .ttl, .nt)

license.name: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 and GNU Free Documentation License (as stated on the DBpedia SPARQL page)

agent_notes: Prefixes such as dbo:, dbr:, rdfs: are predefined on the public endpoint. Always add LIMIT; one response is cut at 10000 rows, use LIMIT/OFFSET with ORDER BY to page. Resource URIs follow http://dbpedia.org/resource/<Wikipedia_title>. Use format=application/sparql-results+json for JSON. For one entity, /data/<Name>.json is simpler than SPARQL.
caveats: Public endpoint is shared; expect timeouts on heavy queries.
Content reflects a periodic extraction from Wikipedia, so it lags the live encyclopedia; for current facts use Wikidata or the Wikipedia API.
The lookup.dbpedia.org search service did not answer in testing, so entity search must be done with SPARQL text filters.

verification.notes: Exact example request executed without a key.
